_comment: Symptom-keyed index of hazards whose explanation ALREADY exists somewhere in this repository. An entry stores no knowledge of its own: it stores the text a person sees when the hazard bites, and a pointer to the record that already explains it. The records stay exactly where their authors put them — next to the cause — and this file makes them reachable from the effect. Read by plugins/src/base/hooks/failure-signature-index.mjs, which runs as a PostToolUse hook on every Bash result (so it is read by the person standing in the symptom, not by anyone who goes looking) and as `bun run check:failure-signatures` (which fails when an entry's record has moved, when its signature no longer matches its own recorded sample, when a row's discriminator has no counterSample proving it discriminates, when a row's determination cannot report a NOT-DETERMINED answer, or when the index resolves nothing at all). A row may only assert what its evidence supports: where one symptom has two opposite causes, `excludes` withholds the row against counter-evidence in the same output and `determination` measures the checkout and reports NOT DETERMINED rather than guessing. See CodySwannGT/lisa#3061 and CodySwannGT/lisa#3812.

entries.symptom: ENOENT on a file under dist/ or plugins/ that is present again seconds later
entries.sample: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/repo/dist/configs/vitest/typescript.d.ts'
entries.cause: a concurrent build deletes dist/ (or plugins/) wholesale before rebuilding it, so every concurrent reader sees a window in which the file does not exist. It is NOT a missing build and NOT a cross-checkout collision.

records.anchor: the integration suite rebuilds dist/ while this runs

guard.anchor: runs a build that never deletes dist
guard.name: the regression test "runs a build that never deletes dist"

entries.symptom: a shell script that works on macOS dies on Linux CI with a syntax error it never reaches the body of
entries.signature: Syntax error: "\(" unexpected|Illegal option -o pipefail|: Bad substitution
entries.cause: /bin/sh is dash on Linux and bash on macOS, so a bash-ism is a parse error before the script executes a single line — including before it reads stdin. The script is not wrong; the interpreter is.

entries.symptom: a merge conflict in a path .gitattributes maps to a custom merge driver, in output where that driver printed its own name
entries.sample: merge-generated-artifact: src/core/upstream-evidence-manifest.ts could not be merged mechanically — both sides changed the entry for scripts/two-channel-couplings.json in incompatible ways.
entries.cause: the driver RAN and DECLINED — it is working as designed. It printed its own diagnosis and the exact commands to resolve, in this same output, above this notice. A driver that is not registered prints nothing at all, so registration is not the question here and `lisa doctor` will not answer it. Scroll up and follow what the driver already told you; `exit 1` means declined here, not failed.

entries.symptom: conflict markers in the project-learnings ledger, which .gitattributes maps to a union merge driver, with NO driver-authored line anywhere in the output
entries.counterSample:
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in .lisa/PROJECT_LEARNINGS.md
merge-learnings: .lisa/PROJECT_LEARNINGS.md: two branches gave one stable id incompatible successors
entries.cause: the ledger conflicted and no driver announced itself. That is consistent with a driver that never ran AND with a driver whose output never reached this transcript, so the two are separated by measuring this checkout rather than by assuming.

determination.question: whether merge.lisa-learnings.driver is registered in this checkout
determination.absent: the merge=lisa-learnings mapping lives in .gitattributes but merge.lisa-learnings.driver is machine-local and unregistered HERE, so git silently fell back to its built-in text merge. Register it with `lisa install-merge-driver` (or any `lisa apply`) run here, then redo the merge. A guard for this already exists — do not build a second one.
determination.present: the driver IS registered here, so an unregistered driver is EXCLUDED. Why it conflicted anyway is NOT MEASURED: no driver line reached this output, and that is not proof one did not run — a killed or timed-out command loses its streams, only the last 512KB of a transcript is read, and `git merge-tree` never runs custom drivers at all. Redo the merge and read the driver's own stderr before naming a cause.
determination.unknown: NOT DETERMINED — this checkout could not be asked whether the driver is registered, so an unregistered driver and a driver that ran with its output lost both remain open. Answer that first with `lisa doctor` and `git config --get merge.lisa-learnings.driver`; do not diagnose past this line.

entries.symptom: conflict markers in a checked-in generated artifact, which .gitattributes maps to a reconstructing merge driver, with NO driver-authored line anywhere in the output
entries.counterSample:
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in src/core/upstream-evidence-manifest.ts
merge-generated-artifact: src/core/upstream-evidence-manifest.ts could not be merged mechanically — both sides changed one entry in incompatible ways.
entries.cause: the artifact conflicted and no driver announced itself. That is consistent with a driver that never ran AND with a driver whose output never reached this transcript, so the two are separated by measuring this checkout rather than by assuming.

determination.question: whether merge.lisa-generated-artifact.driver is registered in this checkout
determination.absent: the merge=lisa-generated-artifact mapping lives in .gitattributes but merge.lisa-generated-artifact.driver is machine-local and unregistered HERE, so git silently fell back to its built-in text merge and the artifact conflicts by construction. Register it by running `bun install` here, then redo the merge. A guard for this already exists — do not build a second one.
determination.present: the driver IS registered here, so an unregistered driver is EXCLUDED. Why it conflicted anyway is NOT MEASURED: no driver line reached this output, and that is not proof one did not run — a killed or timed-out command loses its streams, only the last 512KB of a transcript is read, and `git merge-tree` never runs custom drivers at all. Redo the merge and read the driver's own stderr before naming a cause.
determination.unknown: NOT DETERMINED — this checkout could not be asked whether the driver is registered, so an unregistered driver and a driver that ran with its output lost both remain open. Answer that first with `lisa doctor` and `git config --get merge.lisa-generated-artifact.driver`; do not diagnose past this line.

records.anchor: Register the `lisa-generated-artifact` merge driver in this checkout's local

entries.symptom: a command reports failure with no assertion, no threshold and no error text
entries.cause: the command was KILLED by a signal on a saturated machine, not answered. It reached no verdict, and its output is a truncated transcript rather than a result — so nothing it printed is a measurement. Re-run it on a quieter machine before reading anything into it.
